newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AMP Investments NZ reports weak March quarter.
newsitem.headline: AMP Investments NZ reports weak March quarter.

text.p: A slowing New Zealand economy and recent rises in U.S. short term interest rates depressed Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Investments returns for the March quarter, the company said on Tuesday.
AMP Investments general manager Roger Greville said the low risk fund returned 0.5 percent, the medium risk fund was negative 0.2 percent and the high risk fund negative 0.6 percent.
That compares with returns in the December quarter for the low risk fund of 4.5 percent, 6.2 percent for the medium risk and 8.1 percent for the high risk.
Greville said returns for the year to the end of March were 9.7 percent for the low and medium risk funds and 10.3 percent for the high risk.
But he said returns comfortably exceeded annual inflation of 1.8 percent, even after allowing for tax.

"Favouring New Zealand assets over much of the year was a key factor in contributing to the good annual managed fund returns. The New Zealand equities, fixed interest and property portfolios all achieved returns of over 10 percent for the year," Greville said.
He said the recent tightening of global liquidity was seen as mildly negative for markets but AMP expected the situation to settle over the next few months.

"New Zealand shares are expected to deliver relatively better returns than global equities or bonds during the year ahead, while an improvement in economic activity later this year will help the equity market in particular," he said.
AMP was also advising clients looking to invest in passive funds not to base their whole investment strategy on tax issues "because tax legislation can change."
